full_judgment: 4. On the objection of the defendants 1 and 2, defendant No. 3, Deputy Collector Central Excise and Land Customs, Rajshahi and defendant No. 4, Pakistan, were impleaded in the suits. The added defendants in their written statement denied liability and stated, inter alia, that the Customs authority detained the consignments on 20.4.57 and requested the Railway to hand over goods so that they might be seized. The railway, however, refused delivery on the ground that the matter had been referred to the higher authority for order. As the consignors contravened I.T.C. Act, 1950 and the Border Trade Agreement in force, the Customs Department formally seized the consignments on 10.6.37 while they were still in custody of the Railway. After the plaintiffs were fined orders were passed permitting them to take delivery of the consignments from the Railway. It was contended by these defendants that the service of notice under section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedures was not proper, valid and legal.
